To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can train an agent on a simulated state input domain and then transfer it to a real world image input domain with a cross-modal domain adaptation method, which is more robust than same-modal domain adaptation methods.
we propose a method to transfer policies from state input to image input, and that our method outperforms current methods designed for domain adaptation with the same input modality.

we propose a cross-modal domain adaptation method that can learn the mapping from high-dimensional image to low-level state, and the policy trained in source domain can be directly transferred to the target domain with the mapping function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of transferring the policy learned in the state domain to the target domain with image inputs.

the problem of cross-modal domain adaptation, where we aim to train a policy on the source domain (e.g., simulator) that can be deployed on the target domain (e.g. real-world) with the same input modality, but a different modality.
the problem of cross-modal domain adaptation for reinforcement learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method can be applied to the problem of cross-modal domain adaptation for reinforcement learning, which is a challenging problem due to the lack of structural constraints from the source to the target domains.

the proposed method can learn a mapping between different modalities, allowing policies trained on state input to transfer directly to image input, and the policy, once integrated with the mapping function can be deployed directly with only a small loss of performance.

our proposed method is able to learn a mapping from the source domain of high-dimensional images to the target domain (low-level simulator states) with the help of the sequential information in trajectories and the policy, allowing agents trained only on the source domain to transfer well to a different domain, while current methods fail on this problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can train policies in a simulator and then directly deploy them to real-world environments without extra training.
we can learn a cross-modal domain adaptation function to transfer the policy trained on state inputs to image inputs, which can significantly reduce the cost of deploying RL agents in practice.
our method is the first to achieve cross-modal transfer in the context of RL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a proper design, RL agents trained on simulated images can achieve comparable performance to the ones trained on the real-world images.
, with a well-learned mapping function, the agent can adapt to a new domain with only a few samples, which is a promising result towards real-world applications.
cross-modal domain adaptation for RL is possible and effective.
